subject: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — data isolation expectations
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alan White <alan.white@finsecure.com>, Jane Doe <jane.doe@finsecure.com>
Date: 2026-06-28T15:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — data isolation expectations

Hi Alan / Jane,

Thanks again for the time earlier today. Quick recap from our side and three quick clarifying questions so we can recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

Recap:
- You walked through the primary SM use cases (customer support ticket summarization + PII redaction on inbound data).
- Key constraint: legal/regulatory team needs strong data isolation and customer control of encryption keys for some data flows.
- Procurement is evaluating Dedicated capacity vs Private VPC (we discussed both).

Questions to confirm:
1) Data residency / tenancy: Will any model inputs or outputs be allowed to leave your VPC boundary (i.e., to Redwood-managed shared network) or do you require that all inference payloads remain exclusively on customer-managed network?
2) KMS / keys: Do you require customer-owned keys (bring-your-own-key / HSM) for at-rest encryption of model caches / logs?
3) Audit & retention: Minimum audit/log retention you need for access and request logs (we typically provide 90 days by default; can extend).

Next steps: If you confirm (1) you need strict VPC-only payload residency + (2) customer-managed keys, the Private VPC/on-prem option is the recommended path. If you can tolerate Redwood-managed compute but need isolation at capacity level, Dedicated might be acceptable and is faster to stand up. I attached our SOC2 summary and a short network diagram to speed the security review.

If it helps, I can put Neha (solutions/security) on a call with your security team — do you have a preferred time next week?

Thanks,

From: Alan White <alan.white@finsecure.com>

Subject: Re: Dedicated vs Private (VPC) — data isolation expectations

Marissa, thanks for the recap, that aligns with our discussion. A few clarifications from our security & procurement side (answered inline):

1) Data residency / tenancy: We require all inference payloads containing customer PII or PHI to remain on our network. That means we cannot have plaintext payloads routed through shared Redwood-managed compute where the tenant co-resides with other customers. If you offer Private VPC with customer-controlled networking (VPC peering / private link) and the ability to host inference nodes inside our VPC or dedicated tenancy, that meets the requirement.

2) KMS / keys: We require BYOK (customer-managed keys) for at-rest encryption of logs and model caches that might contain derived or transient PII. HSM-backed keys preferred.

3) Audit & retention: We need 12 months of immutable access logs for all inference requests and management actions. We also need the ability to export logs to our SIEM (S3/HTTPS endpoint).

Other questions:
- Does Redwood's control plane ever see raw request/response payloads for Private VPC deployments? We need a guarantee that for Private config the control plane only handles orchestration metadata and that payloads are never stored outside our environment.
- For Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools), is there any shared multi-tenant network path by default, or can we configure strict network isolation? We're evaluating cost vs timeline; procurement asked for a high-level comparison (security delta + rough timeline to production).

I've attached our security questionnaire (FinSecure_Security_Questions.xlsx) that procurement wants completed. Also copying procurement lead Jane for timeline coordination.

Thanks,

Marissa, summary below you can forward to Alan / Jane. TL;DR: Private (customer VPC) is the recommended path given the requirements; Dedicated can be an interim option with caveats.

1) Control plane / payload access:
- Private VPC: We support a private deployment where inference nodes run in customer-managed VPCs via VPC peering or PrivateLink. In this configuration, request/response payloads never traverse Redwood-managed shared compute or storage; the control plane handles orchestration metadata only (job scheduling, health checks) and does not retain raw payloads. We can provide a written attestation and architecture diagram for contracts.
- Dedicated: Reserved GPU pools in Redwood-managed VPCs are isolated at the tenant level (no multi-tenant compute on the same instance), but networking is still routed through Redwood-managed infrastructure by default. We can offer stricter network isolation (dedicated tenancy + private link) but that requires additional network configuration and may not meet BYOK/HSM requirements for customer key ownership of platform-level caches.

2) KMS / BYOK / HSM:
- Private VPC: Customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported. We can integrate with AWS KMS using customer keys or an HSM appliance depending on the deployment. Model caches and logs can be encrypted with customer keys and we can surface encryption proofs for audits.
- Dedicated: We support encrypted caches; however, BYOK for platform-managed caches is limited unless we stand up a customer-dedicated key integration for the account (adds time).

3) Audit logs & retention / SIEM export:
- We can export audit and request logs to the customer's S3 bucket or SIEM endpoint. Default retention is 90 days; for Private deployments we can configure 12+ months retention (immutable logging via WORM on S3) as part of the deployment scope.

4) Timeline / recommended next steps:
- Private VPC POC: 4–6 weeks to stand up a small POC environment (networking validation, key integration, and audit export). Requires FinSecure networking contact + SIEM/S3 details + signing a DoD/Network addendum.
- Dedicated quickstart: 2–3 weeks to provision reserved capacity and perform validation; additional 2–4 weeks for BYOK/HSM integration if required.

5) Pricing & procurement notes:
- Private VPC has a higher implementation and operational fee due to dedicated networking and key management integration. We will provide a delta sheet (POC vs production) for procurement.

Attachments to include in reply to customer: redwood_soc2_summary.pdf, network_diagram.png, and an architecture attestation doc (I can draft).

Next step I recommend: Introduce our solutions architect (Vivek) to FinSecure's network lead and schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week.
